CORRECTED from original PASS classification, which mistakenly treated this as a property-holding REIT. MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF) is actually a government-backed mortgage lending vehicle, not a rental-property trust - its core business is originating fixed-rate mortgage loans to homebuyers at a stated 9.75% interest rate (well below commercial bank rates of 18-22%), plus construction financing guarantees to developers, with repayments recycled into new loans. Interest-bearing lending is the core product, not an incidental tenant-mix issue like genuine property REITs (NREIT, UPDCREIT, SFSREIT, UHOMREIT) - same category as the mortgage banks (INFINITY, LIVINGTRUST) already marked FAIL.

Core activities (oil palm, poultry, fish farming, feed milling, crop cultivation, snail farming) are permissible, but the company's own NGX listing announcement names piggery among its stated business lines - swine farming is a categorical exclusion regardless of revenue share. Current public-facing materials (company site, most profiles) omit piggery, so current materiality is unconfirmed - needs direct segment-revenue check in latest annual report/prospectus. Separately, NGX suspended trading and opened an investigation into the stock after an 859% one-month price surge - a governance/integrity risk independent of the halal screen.

Vetiva Griffin 30 ETF - tracks the NGX 30 Index, which holds conventional (interest-based) banks (Zenith Bank, GTCO, UBA, etc.) and other companies that fail the business-activity screen directly as portfolio constituents; a Shariah-compliant investor cannot look through to only the permissible names inside a passively-replicated index fund.

NewGold ETF - each unit represents a claim on physical gold bullion held in a vault, and gold itself is a permissible asset. However, AAOIFI Shariah Standard No. 57 requires immediate/constructive possession and same-session settlement for gold trades to avoid riba al-fadl/gharar; whether NewGold's custodial and settlement structure (allocated vs unallocated bullion, T+ settlement cycle) satisfies this needs direct confirmation from the fund's trust deed before resolving to a clean PASS.
Stanbic IBTC ETF 30 - tracks the same NGX 30 Index as VETGRIF30, so it directly holds conventional banks and other impermissible constituents as core portfolio holdings.

Vetiva Banking ETF - tracks the NGX Banking Index, i.e. a basket of the top 10 conventional (interest-based) banks listed on NGX; a dedicated sector fund investing exclusively in an impermissible activity.

Vetiva Consumer Goods ETF - tracks the NGX Consumer Goods Index (top 15 Food/Beverage/Tobacco companies by market cap). Index composition is not confirmed here, but this sector historically includes brewers (Nigerian Breweries, Guinness, International Breweries) alongside permissible food/personal-care names - constituent weights need verification before resolving to PASS or FAIL.

Vetiva Industrial ETF - tracks the NGX Industrial Index (top 10 Industrial Goods companies). The sector is dominated by cement, paints, and building-materials manufacturers that generally pass a standalone business-activity screen, but the exact constituent list and weights are unconfirmed here, so a full PASS is not yet warranted.

Greenwich Alpha ETF - tracks the broad NGX All-Share Index, which includes conventional banks, insurers, breweries and other impermissible names as core constituents alongside permissible companies; a market-cap-weighted all-share tracker cannot exclude these holdings.

Meristem Growth ETF - tracks a growth-oriented basket of NGX-listed equities (Meristem Growth Index). Public disclosures reviewed here don't specify the constituent list; growth indices on NGX have historically spanned multiple sectors including financial services, so sector exposure needs verification before resolving to PASS or FAIL.

Meristem Value ETF - tracks a value-oriented basket of NGX-listed equities (Meristem Value Index); same open question as MERGROWTH - constituent sector mix needs verification before resolving to PASS or FAIL.

Vetiva S&P Nigeria Sovereign Bond ETF - holds a basket of Federal Government of Nigeria bonds and generates its return from fixed coupon (interest) income; a conventional fixed-income instrument, which is riba by definition.

SIAML Pension ETF 40 - tracks the NGX Pension Index (top 40 pension-fund-eligible companies across all sectors), which includes conventional banks and insurers as core constituents; a broad-based tracker cannot exclude these impermissible holdings.

Core aviation ground/cargo/passenger handling and logistics lines (NAHCO FTZ, Commodities, Logistics, Power Solutions, Aviation Academy) are clean fee-for-service businesses. However, NAHCO Travel and Hospitality Limited (NHTL) now directly operates Sapphire Hotel, a 20-room in-terminal hotel at MMIA Terminal II (opened Feb 2026), with an on-site restaurant/lounge. No alcohol service confirmed either way in public disclosures - amenities described (breakfast, lunch/dinner, business office, gym, prayer area). Predominantly permissible core business.

Lotus Halal Equity ETF, managed by Lotus Capital - explicitly tracks the NGX-Lotus Islamic Index, which is pre-screened to exclude conventional banks, insurance, alcohol, gambling and other impermissible activities, with financial-ratio screening (debt, cash, interest income) built into index eligibility. The only NGX-listed equity ETF designed from inception to be Shariah-compliant.
